technologies.name: eBPF
technologies.what: Executes sandboxed bytecode inside the Linux kernel without modifying kernel source code.
technologies.why: It enables programmable zero-overhead packet filtering, syscall tracing, and real-time security auditing.
technologies.where: Linux kernel tracing, Cilium networking, Falco security auditing, and socket performance profiling.
technologies.when: Use when kernel-level observability, network packet filtering, or syscall enforcement is required at line rate.
technologies.how: C/Rust eBPF programs, BPF maps, helpers, kprobes, tracepoints, and clang target bpf compilation.

technologies.name: OpenQASM 3.0
technologies.what: Describes quantum circuits, entanglement gates, and classical feedback loops for QPUs.
technologies.why: It provides a hardware-agnostic intermediate representation for gate-based quantum compilation.
technologies.where: IBM Quantum, AWS Braket, Rigetti, QPU simulators, and quantum error correction algorithms.
technologies.when: Use when constructing quantum circuits, Bell states, or hybrid quantum-classical algorithms.
technologies.how: Qubit declarations, Hadamard/CNOT gates, measurement registers, and real-time classical conditionals.

technologies.name: Cairo
technologies.what: A Turing-complete language for writing STARK-provable programs and zero-knowledge verification logic.
technologies.why: It allows complex off-chain execution to be mathematically proven on-chain via succinct cryptographic receipts.
technologies.where: Starknet, STARK-based L2 rollups, verifiable AI inference, and privacy-preserving audit ledgers.
technologies.when: Use when off-chain state execution must produce cryptographically verifiable proof of correctness.
technologies.how: Felt types, memory alignment, hint execution, Sierra lowering, and STARK proof verification.

technologies.name: JAX (xAI Grok Flagship)
technologies.what: Autograd and XLA compiler framework for high-performance functional neural network compute.
technologies.why: Powering Grok (xAI) and Gemini models with functional purity, automatic differentiation, and XLA kernel compilation.
technologies.where: Grok LLM training pipelines, xAI cluster orchestration, TPU/GPU distributed attention, and neural dynamics.
technologies.when: Use when building high-performance LLMs (Grok-scale), custom automatic differentiation, or XLA-compiled tensor transforms.
technologies.how: jax.jit, jax.grad, jax.vmap, jax.pmap, flax/equinox modules, NamedSharding, and PartitionSpec XLA lowering.

technologies.name: Soufflé Datalog
technologies.what: Declarative logic programming language for high-speed static code analysis and security verification.
technologies.why: It resolves complex graph reachability, pointer analysis, and security policy rules in parallel C++ code.
technologies.where: Vulnerability scanning, compiler program analysis, access control evaluation, and static call graph analysis.
technologies.when: Use when declarative rule-based query evaluation across large code graphs is required.
technologies.how: Facts, relations, horn clauses, stratification, fixed-point evaluation, and C++ compilation.

technologies.name: RHL-Quant (1.58b Ternary Quantization Flagship)
technologies.what: Post-training 2-level quantum-lattice quantization engine combining 1.58-bit ternary base with 2-bit sparse residual delta HLO mesh.
technologies.why: Shrinks 314-billion parameter LLM weights (Grok-1) from 628 GB down to ~65 GB, enabling full 314B MoE inference on a single 80GB H100 GPU.
technologies.where: Frontier LLM deployment, VRAM constrained edge clusters, bitwise GPU matrix multiplication, and ultra-low memory inference.
technologies.when: Use when fitting massive MoE or dense LLMs onto minimal GPU VRAM hardware without perplexity degradation.
technologies.how: Base ternary lattice {-1, 0, +1}, residual delta mesh, POPCNT bitwise GPU matmul, and dynamic scale factor reconstruction.
